# The capped simplex angular surplus: complete dependency graph

## Precise statement

For d>=3, let E_0,...,E_d be independent mean-one exponential variables and let

    a_0=-1,   -1<=a_i<=1,   sum_(i=0)^d a_i=0.

Write Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. The separately proved scalar theorem is

    (L) For every integer k>=1 and p in[0,1],
        Pr(Gamma(k)+p Exp(1)>=Exp(1)+k+p-1)>=9/20,

with all variables in (L) independent. Together with the proved reductions
below, it implies the unconditional bound

    Pr(sum_(i=0)^d a_i E_i>=0) >= (7/6) Gamma_d.      (1)

The proof of (L) is now complete in
`candidate 93a759825a881af9`.
Independent full audits are recorded in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)` and
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.
Its conclusion is in fact strict. No scalar hypothesis remains.

Equivalently, for the standard simplex

    T_d={x in R^d: x_i>=0, sum_i x_i<=1},

its centroid g=(1/(d+1),...,1/(d+1)), and every normal u satisfying

    u_i>=0,    sum_i u_i=1,    max_i u_i<=2/(d+1),

one has

    vol_d({x in T_d: u dot x>=1/(d+1)})
        >=(7/6) Gamma_d vol_d(T_d).                   (2)

This is an angular statement for a restricted simplex normal cone. It is not OC, and makes no assertion of the factor7/6 in dimensions d=1 or d=2.

## Dependency graph

Each node below has a complete proof in the named source. There is no
unproved leaf in this auxiliary angular theorem's dependency graph.

0. The deterministic-negative fractional gamma bound (L):
   `candidate 93a759825a881af9`.
   Its analytic large-index bound and exact finite interval certificates
   cover every integer k and every real p in[0,1]. It uses none of nodes1-7.

1. The log-concave reciprocal-Laplace and size-bias Hessian identities:
   `candidate 8704554a92158bfc`.
2. The geometric conditional-mean/mode lemma, integer-Gamma density derivative sign, and saturated-positive negative equalization:
   `candidate a6e6fd61fe60c16a`.
3. Compact minimizers and their boundary-stratum classification, using nodes1-2:
   `candidate 9dace055ddbb6578`.
   A nonsaturated minimizing pattern is (1^k,p) against (1,b^m), with 0<p,b<1, k+p=1+mb, and no zero coordinates. Thus k+m=d-1.
4. The exact stationary second-variation exclusion, using nodes1 and3:
   `candidate 9cac770b3cc82243`.
   A fractional minimum below1/2 must have p>b, hence m>k.
5. The three endpoint theorems for that fractional family:
   `candidate a0a6a51e2d3624e9` (k=1),
   `candidate ea3c1d3cbe80cfbc` (k=2, repaired quintic certificate),
   `candidate 5d115e607fe36eb9` (k=3).
   All three hold for every admissible number m of negative phases, and give an endpoint minimum in p in[0,1].
6. The dimension-free escape implication, using nodes2-3 and (L):
   `candidate a21ff89aef880b49`.
   It proves probability>=9/20 in every dimension, by compact minima and explicit control of both escaping indices; it does not assume an infinite-dimensional minimum exists.
7. The finite exact saturated probabilities, their minima for d=3,...,9, and the final constants are proved below.

The source `candidate 49f9fad7c4bf7e35` supplies an independently useful uniform bound for saturated positives. For the implication in node6 it is enough to use node2 and the p=0 instance of(L), so no extra unproved uniform estimate is a dependency.

## Exact saturated probabilities

Suppose k positive coefficients equal one. There are at most q=d-k remaining negative coefficients besides the fixed negative unit. Pad their vector with zeros to length q. Since their total is k-1 and each is at most one, admissibility forces 1<=k<=floor((d+1)/2). Node2 proves that their probability is at least

    B_(d,k)=Pr(Gamma(k)>=Exp(1)+[(k-1)/q]Gamma(q)).

For d>=3 the denominator q+k-1=d-1 is positive. Let

    z=(k-1)/(q+k-1).

The exact value is

    B_(d,k)=(1/2)(q/(q+k-1))^q
        sum_(l=0)^(k-1) sum_(j=0)^l
          binom(q+j-1,j) z^j 2^(-(l-j)).             (3)

To prove (3), use the integer-shape gamma survival
Pr(Gamma(k)>=y)=e^(-y) sum_(l=0)^(k-1)y^l/l!. The Laplace transform of the negative sum at one is (1/2)(q/(q+k-1))^q. Exponential tilting changes its component means to1/2 and z repeated q times. The l-th moment divided by l! is the complete homogeneous polynomial in those means, namely sum_(j=0)^l binom(q+j-1,j)z^j 2^(-(l-j)). This proves (3), also at k=1, where z=0 and the value is1/2.

For d=3,...,9, all admissible values are listed in increasing order of k:

|d|B_(d,1), B_(d,2), ..., B_(d,floor((d+1)/2))|
|---|---|
|3|1/2, 1/2|
|4|1/2, 13/27|
|5|1/2, 243/512, 1/2|
|6|1/2, 1472/3125, 12177/25000|
|7|1/2, 21875/46656, 350/729, 1/2|
|8|1/2, 384912/823543, 3134375/6588344, 404112/823543|
|9|1/2, 15647317/33554432, 61965/131072, 16265625/33554432, 1/2|

These are exact evaluations of the finite sums (3). Their minima, denoted mu_d, are the k=2 entries, with a tie at d=3.

## Exact minimum for every d=3,...,9

Take a compact coefficient minimizer. If it is in the all-unit-negative stratum, its probability is at least1/2>=mu_d. If it has only unit positive coefficients, node2 and (3) give at leastmu_d.

Otherwise node3 puts it in the fractional pattern with k+m=d-1. If its probability is at least1/2 there is nothing further to prove. If it is less than1/2, node4 gives m>k. Since d<=9, this forces k<=3. Node5 therefore bounds it by the smaller endpoint value in p. At p=0 the positive fractional coordinate becomes zero; it may be included as one more padded negative zero when applying node2. At p=1 it becomes an additional positive unit. In either case node2 bounds the endpoint below by an admissible B_(d,k') and hence by mu_d. Thus every minimizer has probability>=mu_d.

Equality is realized by two positive units, the mandatory negative unit, and q=d-2 equal negative magnitudes1/q. Consequently mu_d is the exact capped coefficient minimum for d=3,...,9; this assertion uses no instance of(L).

The exact margins over the target are

|d|mu_d-(7/6)Gamma_d|
|---|---|
|3|1/128|
|4|61/16875|
|5|2147/373248|
|6|439904/52521875|
|7|32753357/3057647616|
|8|1348942633648/106352477257509|
|9|939511987337/65536000000000|

Every numerator and denominator is positive. `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_capped_angular_low_dimension_constants.py` checks all evaluations, comparisons, and margins in exact rational arithmetic.

## All d>=10 from the dimension-free implication

By the proved (L), node6 gives probability>=9/20. The sequence Gamma_d decreases: for real x>0,

    d/dx [x log(x/(x+1))]
       =-log(1+1/x)+1/(x+1)<0,

using log(1+t)>t/(1+t) for t>0, which follows by integrating the derivative t/(1+t)^2 of their difference from zero. Therefore, for d>=10,

    (7/6)Gamma_d <= (7/6)(10/11)^10 <9/20,

with exact margin at ten

    9/20-(7/6)(10/11)^10
       =310464227/1556245476060>0.

This proves (1) in all d>=10; the preceding section proves it for
d=3,...,9. The full angular statement is therefore unconditional.

## Equivalence with the simplex cap statement

Let G=sum_(i=0)^d E_i. The vector (E_1/G,...,E_d/G) is uniform on T_d: changing variables from the positive E_i to G and the barycentric coordinates has Jacobian G^d, and the joint density factors into the gamma density of G and a constant simplex density.

Given u as in (2), define a_0=-1 and a_i=(d+1)u_i-1. These coefficients lie in[-1,1] and sum to zero. Since G>0,

    u dot(E_1/G,...,E_d/G)>=1/(d+1)
    iff sum_(i=0)^d a_i E_i>=0.

Conversely every coefficient vector in (1) gives such a normal by u_i=(a_i+1)/(d+1). This proves the equivalence. The closed boundary has zero d-volume because u is nonzero, and the exponential representation also has no atom at zero owing to the fixed -E_0 term. Thus the inequalities concern the stated closed halfspaces without an omitted boundary-mass convention.
